idempotency_key.description: Optional client-supplied key. Requests repeated with the same key are executed at most once.

args.title: checkout-api v2.3.1 failing health checks; rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary: After the deploy of checkout-api v2.3.1 to production, the service started failing health checks in all regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west), with an error rate of 18%. v2.3.1 was also unhealthy in staging as v2.3.1-rc. The SRE agent rolled checkout-api back in all production regions to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production. After the rollback, all regions run v2.3.0, the service is healthy, and the error rate is about 0.2%. Next steps: find the root cause in v2.3.1 and look at why the release went to production after failing in staging.

trace.final:
I rolled checkout-api back to v2.3.0 in all regions, and it's healthy again. I also opened SEV2 incident INC-0001, which paged the on-call engineer.

1. **Before:** v2.3.1 was running in all three regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west), failing health checks with an 18% error rate. It had also failed in staging as v2.3.1-rc before it went to production.
2. **Version chosen:** the release history shows v2.3.0 is the most recent release that was healthy in production. Because it has been healthy in production before, it didn't need change-manager approval.
3. **Rollback:** all three regions now run v2.3.0. A follow-up status check shows the service healthy with about a 0.2% error rate.
4. **Incident:** the first attempt to open it timed out. The incident list was still empty, so I retried with the same deduplication key, which can't create a second incident. The retry worked, and the list now shows exactly one: INC-0001. Its summary covers the failure, the rollback and the next steps: find the root cause in v2.3.1, and find out why it reached production after failing in staging.
